To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the COVID 19 outbreak has highlighted the need to further centralise macroprudential powers and authorities within the ECB.
the SSM has been able to implement a number of important macroprudential measures to mitigate the negative impact of the COVID 10 crisis on the banking sector.
the Single Supervision Mechanism is not working properly and that the powers and authorities of the ECB should be extended to the field of macroprudentials.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How did the ECB and the national competent authorities respond to the COVID 19 outbreak? How did they implement specific measures to offer capital and/or liquidity relief to banks? What is the impact of the measures implemented? Are the measures consistent with the objectives of macroprudental supervision? Are they consistent with the objectives and principles of microprudential supervision? What are the consequences of the measures implemented in respect of the allocation of powers between macro and microprudental authorities?
the following questions: (i) what is the role of the SSM in the current pandemic crisis; (ii) how can the SSM be further improved to better deal with the current crisis and to avoid future crises?
the following questions: 1. How did the ECB and the NCAs respond in the context of the COVID-19 crisis to the capital and liquidity needs of banks?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ECB should be the sole macroprudential supervisor and that the national competent authorities should be the microprudential supervisors, but that the ECB should have the power to override the decisions of the national competent authorities.
the COVID-19 pandemic and the measures taken in response to it have shown that the SSM is not fully equipped for the challenges of the future and that it should be further reformed.
there is a lack of uniformity and transparency in the implementation of measures to provide relief to banks during the COVID 10 pandemic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the COVID-19 crisis has shown the need for more centralisation of powers within the SSM, especially with regards to macroprudential policy.

the ECB should be granted the authority to implement macroprudential measures in all Member States, while the national competent authorities should be granted the power to implement macroprudent measures in the national jurisdiction.

the COVID 19 measures taken by the ECB and National Competent Authorities have not been coordinated, which has led to divergent and sometimes even contradictory measures, and that a centralisation with the Single Supervisory Board of macroprudental powers would have been beneficial.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ECB and the NCA’s should be able to use the same instruments and tools to support the financial system.
the SSM needs to be strengthened in order to ensure a more harmonious and uniform implementation of measures in the future.
the COVID 19 measures have highlighted that the current macroprudential framework is insufficiently equipped to deal with the COVID 19 shock.
